objective_text: Verify logical equivalence using truth tables

questions.stem: Determine if the following two propositions are logically equivalent: (A ∧ B) → C and ¬A ∨ (B → C)
questions.solution:
To verify logical equivalence, we construct a truth table for both propositions and compare them. The two propositions are logically equivalent if their truth values match in every row of the truth table.
Truth Table for (A ∧ B) → C:
| A  | B  | C  |  (A ∧ B)  |  (A ∧ B) → C  |
|---|---|---|--------|-------------|
| T  | T  | T  |   T     |     T        |
| T  | T  | F  |   T     |     F        |
| T  | F  | T  |   F     |     T        |
| T  | F  | F  |   F     |     T        |
| F  | T  | T  |   F     |     T        |
| F  | T  | F  |   F     |     T        |
| F  | F  | T  |   F     |     T        |
| F  | F  | F  |   F     |     T        |

Truth Table for ¬A ∨ (B → C):
| A  | B  | C  | ¬A  | B → C  | ¬A ∨ (B → C)  |
|---|---|---|----|-------|-------------|
| T  | T  | T  |  F  |   T    |      T       |
| T  | T  | F  |  F  |   F    |      F       |
| T  | F  | T  |  F  |   T    |      T       |
| T  | F  | F  |  F  |   T    |      T       |
| F  | T  | T  |  T  |   T    |      T       |
| F  | T  | F  |  T  |   F    |      T       |
| F  | F  | T  |  T  |   T    |      T       |
| F  | F  | F  |  T  |   T    |      T       |

Comparing the truth tables, we can see that both propositions have the same truth values in every row. Therefore, they are logically equivalent.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C: ¬(A ∧ B) ∨ C, which is the contrapositive of (A ∧ B) → C and is logically equivalent to it.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing D: ¬A ∧ (B → C). This choice represents a different proposition that is not logically equivalent to the original pair. It has different truth values in some rows, which means it does not preserve the same logical relationship.

Truth Table for (p ∨ q) ∧ ¬q:
| p  | q  |  (p ∨ q)  | ¬q  |  (p ∨ q) ∧ ¬q  |

| T  | T  |   T     |  F  |      F       |
| T  | F  |   T     |  T  |      T       |
| F  | T  |   T     |  F  |      F       |
| F  | F  |   F     |  T  |      F       |

Truth Table for p → (q → p):
| p  | q  | p → (q → p)  |
|---|---|-------------|
| T  | T  |      T       |

| F  | F  |      T       |

Comparing the truth tables, we can see that both propositions have the same truth values in every row. Therefore, they are logically equivalent.
